title: Patron's Guide: The Collection Charge Where There Is No Grain Money to Draw a Buyout From
content:
**Why is a collection charge added at all?** The collection charge on Grain Marketing Contracts covers recovering the buyout where there is no grain money to draw it from.

**When is it added, and how much?**

- Where no settlement statement stands on the contract to draw the charge on and the member's crop input account under Crop Input Purchasing Accounts stands past due or suspended, the collection charge is 60.00.
- Where no settlement statement stands on the contract to draw the charge on but the crop input account stands in neither of those standings, the collection charge is 25.00.
- Where a settlement statement stands on the contract, no collection charge is added.

**Which is read first?** Whether a settlement statement stands on the contract. Where one does, nothing is added whatever the standing of the crop input account. Only where none stands does the standing of that account, held under Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, decide between 60.00 and 25.00.

**A hypothetical case.** A contract with no settlement statement standing against it, held by a member whose crop input account is suspended, carries a collection charge of 60.00. The same contract, held by a member whose crop input account stands in good order, carries 25.00. Where a settlement statement stands on the contract, the buyout carries no collection charge at all, whatever the input account shows.
